name: Persistent Spinal Pain Syndrome Type 2 / Failed Back Surgery Syndrome
tags: persistent spinal pain syndrome type 2 / failed back surgery syndrome
definition: Persistent or recurrent spinal and/or radicular pain after one or more spinal operations, now often termed persistent spinal pain syndrome type 2.

typical: Persistent back or leg pain after surgery

investigations.principle: Imaging is cause-directed and may include MRI with contrast, CT or dynamic radiographs depending on prior surgery.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, cartilage, occult injury, postoperative or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Repeat surgery should be based on a clearly correctable structural cause, not pain alone.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Chronic Vata-pain phenotype may be documented only as a parallel layer.

patientEducation.summary: Persistent or recurrent spinal and/or radicular pain after one or more spinal operations, now often termed persistent spinal pain syndrome type 2.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, respiratory distress, progressive neurological deficit, open injury, severe deformity, infection or other listed red flags.
